questions.q: Consider that you need to measure the impedance of a coaxial cable. Can you use the property of terminal reflection for this purpose? Is this method feasible?

explain.text: When the terminal is matched, there is no reflection. This method can be used to measure the impedance of a coaxial cable; therefore, this method is correct.

questions.q: Consider that you need to measure the impedance of a coaxial cable. Is it feasible to do so by measuring the attenuation of the signal in the cable?

explain.text: Measuring the attenuation of the signal can provide some information about the coaxial cable, but it is not the most effective method for directly measuring impedance. Therefore, this method is generally not used to measure impedance.

questions.q: Consider if you need to measure the impedance of a coaxial cable. Can it be measured directly using an ohmmeter?

explain.text: Using an ohmmeter to directly measure the impedance of a coaxial cable is not accurate because the ohmmeter measures direct current (DC) resistance, while the characteristic impedance of a coaxial cable is an alternating current (AC) parameter. Therefore, this method is not recommended.
